newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-PIRATES OUTPITCH WHITE SOX AGAIN.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-PIRATES OUTPITCH WHITE SOX AGAIN.

text.p: (Interleague games in National League parks)
Jason Schmidt threw a five-hitter to cap an impressive display of Pirate pitching as Pittsburgh completed a three-game sweep of the visiting Chicago White Sox with a 3-1 win Wednesday.
Schmidt got his second straight complete game and third consecutive win as Pirate pitchers limited Chicago to two runs and 15 hits while striking out 28 in the interleague series.
"We pitched great in the series," said Bucs manager Gene Lamont.

Schmidt (4-4) walked one, recorded a season-high 10 strikeouts and came within one out of his first career shutout. He has given up just three runs and 14 hits in his last three starts, spanning 25 innings.
"Everybody's just in a groove right now," Schmidt said. "It was nice to get a complete game last week and to have back-to-back is something special."
The 24-year-old right-hander blanked Chicago until Albert Belle doubled home Ray Durham with two out in the top of the ninth.
Pittsburgh starters pitched all but one inning of the series against a White Sox team that averaged more than seven runs in its previous seven games.
Chicago's Jaime Navarro (6-7) allowed three runs -- two earned -- and six hits in seven innings. The loss dropped the White Sox below .500 at 40-41.
"Good pitching again tonight, their pitchers were just better," Chicago manager Terry Bevington said. "Navarro had a nice game but Schmidt was devastating."
Dale Sveum put Pittsburgh ahead to stay in the second when he drilled a 2-0 pitch from Navarro 428 feet down the right-field line into the fourth level at Three Rivers Stadium.

In San Francisco, Mark McGwire hit his major league-leading 30th homer and Scott Spiezio added a two-run shot in a six-run fifth as the Oakland Athletics defeated the Giants 8-1 in the first meeting between the teams since the earthquake-delayed World Series of 1989.
"You can feel it," Spiezio said of the Bay Area rivalry. "It means a little bit more than the rest of the interleague games. It sounded like a pretty even crowd."
Tony Batista also homered for the A's, who have won six of their last nine games.
It is the eighth time McGwire has hit 30 homers in a season, surpassing Jimmie Foxx for the franchise record. The Giants have surrendered 17 home runs in their last six games.

In St Louis, Willie McGee homered off Eddie Guardado (0-3) with one out in the bottom of the 10th as the Cardinals (41-41) reached the .500 mark for the first time this season with a 2-1 victory over the Minnesota Twins.

Mark Petkovsek (4-4) got the win with two scoreless innings in relief of Alan Benes, who allowed one run over eight innings with 10 strikeouts. Benes has allowed one earned run in each of his last four starts, but is just 1-2 in that span.

In Chicago, Sammy Sosa homered and drove in a pair of runs and Kevin Foster won his 10th game of the season to lead the Cubs to a 3-2 victory over the Kansas City Royals and a sweep of their three-game interleague series.
Foster (10-5) allowed one run over 6 1/3 innings and has won seven of his last nine decisions. Kevin Appier (6-6) was the loser.

Mark Grace, the Cubs' All-Star representative, had an RBI single but made two errors in the eighth inning, his first multi-error game since May 1992, and fouled a ball off his foot that required him to make a trip to a hospital.

In Cincinnati, Bret Boone snapped the worst hitless slump of his career with a two-run single in a three-run fourth and Brett Tomko (5-1) won his fifth straight decision as the Reds completed a three-game sweep of the Milwaukee Brewers, 7-4.

Boone, who was hitless in his previous 26 at-bats, pulled a single into left field, scoring Hal Morris and Joe Oliver for a 3-1 lead. Boone, who was sent down to the minors earlier this season by manager Ray Knight, is still batting only .195 with two homers and 23 RBI.
In Houston, Mike Hampton scattered 10 hits in his first complete game in just over a year as the Astros beat the Cleveland Indians 6-2.

Hampton (4-7), who has allowed three runs or less in each of his last four starts, had just one hit in 32 previous at-bats but broke open a 1-0 game with a two-run triple in the fifth. Craig Biggio, Chuck Carr and Jeff Bagwell added RBI later in the frame.
The Astros had three triples, tying a club record last accomplished in 1981.
In San Diego, Rickey Henderson hit a first-inning leadoff home run and an eighth-inning three-run double and Chris Gomez had a two-run homer as the Padres beat the Seattle Mariners 8-5.
Joey Hamilton (6-3) allowed three runs and nine hits over seven innings. Jeff Fassero (8-4) took the loss.
Edgar Martinez hit a solo homer in the ninth for Seattle.
